dct_title_s: Il regno della servia detta altrimenti rascia / descritto da Giacomo Cantelli.
dct_description_sm: Relief shown pictorially.; "The map is centered on the upper Morava River and includes a wide swath of territory from eastern Dalmatia and Bosnia across Rascia to the Danube, and from the Hungarian plain southward to the mountainous borderlands of Macedonia and Albania. Cantelli's distinctive style of clustered hill shading for topography, turreted symbols for towns and fortresses, and a clearly structured system of rivers and roads provides a military and logistical reading of the landscape. At lower left is an elaborate decorative cartouche bearing the title, flanked by trophies of arms and surmounted by a large eagle, displaying the Serbian imperial device grappling with an Ottoman crescent moon"--Ruderman.; "At lower left is an elaborate decorative cartouche bearing the title, flanked by trophies of arms and surmounted by a large eagle, displaying the Serbian imperial device grappling with an Ottoman crescent moon. At upper right, an ornate dedication cartouche with floral ornamentation frames the arms of Cardinal Alfonso Michele Litta (1608-1679), Archbishop of Milan from 1652 until his death. Although Litta had died a decade earlier, the map is posthumously dedicated to him in recognition of his ecclesiastical prominence and patronage"--Ruderman.
